area.title: A task's budget counts everything spent on it (its work, the critic's reviews and the fixes after a review) as one figure. Its runs and its reviews stop at that figure. A work run keeps room for its review when the budget can hold it. A review that does not fit pauses cleanly with the work kept, and one Continue gives it what it needs. The estimate includes the review, the plan card equals the Start dialog, and the screens and the session review set one figure against the budget and the estimate (the owner's answer of 2026-11-16, which replaces run L3's work-only default)
problems: [major] BA-1: A task's own figure (actual_cost_usd_micro, which its budget, its cards and Continue read) holds only the specialist's work. The critic's reviews are booked in the ledger, the session and Costs > By task, but never on the task, so a task's cost reads higher than its budget (live check 3: 'CHF 0.13 of CHF 0.20 budget' while the run could spend CHF 0.11). Owner: "yes it should count critics reviews, and fixes." Where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2428-2436 (recordStep: task.addCost per model step) and :2551 (the rest at the run's end), the work path only; :4341-4439 (reviewTask puts outcome.costUsdMicro on the critic.verdict event only, :4436); packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:2456 (lateRunCost); packages/state/src/schema.ts:230 ('Reviews are not in it').

[major] BA-2: Every task written so far has a figure without its past reviews, although the ledger holds them under its task id (the critic's token carries it: packages/critic/src/critic.ts:496-516; every call books a ledger row: packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:262-283). After the change, new spend and old spend would follow two rules. Owner: "yes it should count critics reviews, and fixes."

[major] BA-3: A task's review is capped only by the session's token, never by what is left of the task's own budget, so its reviews can take its spend past its budget. A run-level refusal reads as the session's budget and ends the session. The refused call's estimate never reaches the card: RunResult.error keeps only code, message, source, level, capUsdMicro, resetAt and sourceId, although the precheck's details carry estimateUsdMicro. Owner: "yes it should count critics reviews, and fixes." and (answer 8) "when the budget will run out, it should be the case that the agent will do as much as it can, and wrap up in an organized and error free way such that the work can be continued in the next run." Where: packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts:686-714 (no budgetUsdMicro); packages/critic/src/critic.ts:507; packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:969-982 (reviewStopSource maps 'run' to 'session'), :2862-2930; packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:376-385, :1104-1113; packages/runtime/src/enforcement/budget.ts:339-348.

[major] BA-4: A work run (a fix after a send-back included) may spend everything left of the task's budget, so once reviews count, a task that works near its budget has no room for its own review. The room must pay what the critic's precheck asks, not only what a review usually costs. Every critic call is checked on its whole input plus 8,192 output tokens (USD 0.082 of output alone on Sonnet 5.5, twice that on Opus), so its first call's worst case is about USD 0.10. A reading review makes several calls, each checked again. The run's cap source is still taken from what is left, not from the run's own cap, so a stop at a cap kept below the session's work budget would read as the session's. Owner: "yes it should count critics reviews, and fixes." / "wrap up in an organized and error free way such that the work can be continued in the next run." Where: packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:696-706 (runCapOf: budget less work), :977-1005 (runCapSource), :1049, :1767-1785; packages/critic/src/critic.ts:134 (REVIEW_TOKENS_PER_CALL), :294 (READING_REVIEW_TURNS 12), :555-557; packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:574-581, :685; packages/billing/src/pricing.ts:104-105; packages/runtime/src/enforcement/budget.ts:318-326 (the session's twin).

[minor] BA-5: Continue on a card at the task's own budget adds 'the same amount again' or the raw stored estimate. The estimate left that the card stores is capped at what is left of the budget, about 0 at such a pause, so it never raises Continue. A waiting review's Continue does not size itself to the review's calls, so the card can come back after Continue. Owner: "such that the work can be continued in the next run." Where: packages/runtime/src/session/budget-card.ts:70-86; packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:4237-4242 (withinTaskBudget(estimateLeftUsdMicro(...))); packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts:980-986.

[major] BA-6: Every estimate counts only the work. The starting figures are documented as 'the work's cost ...; the critic's review is paid from the session's review reserve'. The learner subtracts the reviews, and estimate() has no review part. So the plan line, the Start dialog, the plan card and the pause card set a whole cost against an estimate of the work alone, and the intake card's stored sentence adds up a third figure (the bounded work guess). Owner: "yes it should count critics reviews, and fixes." (reading: its estimate includes the reviews and fixes). Where: packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts:146-169, :388-443, :456-462, :615-652; packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts:1453-1457, :1466-1472, :1491, :2709-2750.

[major] BA-7: The live learner samples a task at task.finished, before its review and once per try. The fold after a restart reads each finished task once, from its final rows. A task can close more than once on the same row (failed is a finished status; Redo and Try again keep the row), and refresh() skips only ids remembered inside a 15-minute window. Once reviews are in the sample, the plan card and the Start dialog would move with a restart (the W15-19 class), and a refresh run inside the process would count a task again. Where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2586-2620 (task.finished, onTaskFinished) vs :2780 (review); packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:2790-2805; packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts:287, :710-720, :736-800, :832-871; packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:1931-1936 and packages/state/src/repos/task.ts:114 (later patches move updated_at).

[major] BA-8: The session review sets the work against the plan's estimate and names the reviews apart ('Session work cost CHF 0.12 exceeded its estimate CHF 0.05 by 140% (the reviews, CHF 0.05 more, are not in the estimate)'; 'the work cost X against an estimate of Y, and the reviews Z'). Once the estimate holds the reviews, this sets two different things against each other. The session's ledger also holds spend that no plan item estimates: C4's task check (task_id null) and the critic's lesson reviews. Owner: "yes it should count critics reviews, and fixes." Where: packages/critic/src/session-review.ts:198, :321-377, :704-716; packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:752-761; git show fix/d1109-selftasks-run:packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts lines 473-490 and 519-539.

[major] BA-9: The Tasks row says the opposite of the owner's answer: 'CHF 0.11 of CHF 0.20 budget left; reviews are not counted' / 'CHF 0.20 budget used up; reviews are not counted', with the tooltip 'Runs of this task stop when the work's spend reaches this budget. The critic's reviews are not counted in it.' The row's spent figure and Costs > By task read the ledger filtered by project. Make one project (C4) leaves a moved task's earlier ledger rows on the closed project, so both read less than its budget counts. Where: apps/ui/src/pages/project/TasksTab.tsx:73-102; packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1102-1106; packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:995-1030; git show fix/d1109-onerepo-join:packages/commands/src/commands/project-join.ts lines 158-163; docs/decisions/0112-a-budget-stop-is-a-clean-pause.md:479-490.

[minor] BA-12: Nothing tells the person that a task's own budget is too small to pay for both its work and its review. Answer 8: "it should get a warning, but it should get done anyway". The Start dialog caps a whole estimate at the budget left (withinTaskBudget) and shows 'about CHF 0.06' with no word that the review will wait. Where: packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts:980-987; packages/runtime/src/session/start-check.ts:190-205.
decisions:
BA-1 One figure per task. Every model call of a task's review is added to the task's actual_cost_usd_micro as the call ends, through task.addCost, the same way as the work's calls (W15-21).
- TaskReviewRequest gains onCost(usdMicro) (append-only, loop/ports.ts:53-70).
- The critic port has one onEvent. It forwards model_call_start to onStarted and each model_call_end's costUsdMicro to onCost, a cut-off call's (CUT_OFF_STOP_REASON) included (agent/loop.ts:794-800, :879-886).
- runner.reviewTask chains the additions, as recordStep chains steps, and awaits them in every branch (verdict, refusal, failure), so each branch reads the whole figure.
- Nothing is added from outcome.costUsdMicro or from a refusal's spentUsdMicro, and the task's version is not bumped.
- Fix runs are work runs and already count.
Result: actual_cost_usd_micro is everything spent on the task (work, every review round, every fix) and equals the ledger's sum for its task id. runCapOf, the cards' spent_usd_micro, Continue's raise (budget-card.ts:361-367), withinTaskBudget, keptWorkFor's gate, the drawer, Costs and C4's task.split then all read that one figure. The session row stays set from the ledger at the session's end. Why: one place per fact (design §5 rule 10).

BA-2 Old tasks follow the same rule. Migration 0010 ('task-spent-all', after C4's 0009) sets each task's actual_cost_usd_micro to the larger of itself and the ledger's sum for its task id. It is data only and idempotent, with SQLite MAX(a, b) and a correlated subquery and Postgres GREATEST, and it changes neither version nor updated_at. A task whose total already passed its budget then pauses before its next run, with today's words and one card with Continue. Why: the budget is what the task costs, one rule for every task, and the ledger has carried the reviews' task id all along, so nothing is guessed.

BA-3 A task's review is capped at what is left of the task's own budget, and a refusal there is the task's budget.
- When the task has a budget of its own, the runner reads the task fresh at the review's start. It passes budgetUsdMicro = budget less the task's figure through TaskReviewRequest.budgetUsdMicro (append-only) to CriticService.review's context; critic.ts:507 already takes the smaller of that and the session token's budget.
- reviewStopSource(level, capSource): a refusal at level 'run' is 'task_budget' when the task's left set the review's cap (left at most the session token's budget), else 'session' as today; 'task', 'project', 'month' and 'plan' map as today.
- Not started: the critic is not started when what is left is below the price of the review's output cap alone on its model: CriticPort.reviewCallUsdMicro(task).floorUsdMicro, 8,192 output tokens, USD 0.082 on Sonnet 5.5 and twice that on Opus. This is a lower bound of its first call. No checks run, no critic Run row is written, and the same pause follows. Between that floor and the real first call, the critic's own precheck refuses as today, after its checks: the same pause.
- The refused call's estimate reaches the card. RunResult.error gains estimateUsdMicro (append-only), copied from details at agent/loop.ts:1104-1113, and refusedReviewError copies it into its details (critic.ts:174-188). Reviews run only on the loop driver (loop/critic.ts:122 'driver: LoopAgentDriver'), so the SDK driver's error shape is not changed.
- Effort max (a tier 3 review on Opus): the first call's output ceiling (MAX_EFFORT_TOKENS_CEILING 24,000) is sized from the run's room (agent/loop.ts:632-653; enforcement/budget.ts:402-417), and that room now also counts what is left of the task's budget. The floor of 8,192 is unchanged. Decided: this is accepted, as the session's room already sizes the ceiling today. BA-4 prices the room at effort max on the ceiling, so a task whose budget keeps room gets the whole ceiling. The prompts and the per-call floor are unchanged.
- Then today's pause applies, unchanged:
  - needs_human with '"X" paused at its budget of CHF 0.06.';
  - the log line '"X" paused before its review: its own budget of CHF 0.06 has no room for it.';
  - one card with review_waits ('The work is done; its review waits for room in the budget.', Continue, Cancel task);
  - keepForReview, and the session goes on (stopEndsSession is false for task_budget).
- After Continue, the next session reviews the kept result without a coder run (W15-27).
- A task without a budget of its own is unchanged: its review stays under the session's token and reserve.
Why: no budget is ever passed, on the whole figure, and a review that does not fit is a clean pause with the work kept (ADR 0112), never a failed try.

BA-4 Each work run, a fix after a send-back included, keeps room for its review when the task's budget can hold it.
- The room needed is reviewRoom = R + W.
  - R is the review part of the task's estimate (BA-6).
  - W is CriticPort.reviewCallUsdMicro(task).worstUsdMicro (append-only port method, built in loop/critic.ts on a new CriticService.reviewCallUsdMicro in critic.ts). It is one critic call's worst case at the task's review tier, with the model and the output cap the review will use: the critic's pickFor(tier, the project's settings) (critic.ts:422-442), and deps.maxTokensPerCall ?? REVIEW_TOKENS_PER_CALL, or MAX_EFFORT_TOKENS_CEILING at effort max. Its input allowance is the critic's system prompt tokens plus REVIEW_EVIDENCE_ALLOWANCE_TOKENS = 8,000. It is priced with the same RunPricing.estimate the loop uses (agent/loop.ts:126, :580): about USD 0.10 on Sonnet 5.5.
  - Why R + W: a reading review makes several calls (READING_REVIEW_TURNS 12), each checked on its worst case. It needs its expected spend plus one call's worst case, ADR 0112's reserve rule for a run that finishes.
- With a task budget, left = budget less the task's figure (BA-1). The room is kept only when reviewRoom is at most half of left, else nothing is kept. workRunCapOf(task, reviewRoom) returns {capUsdMicro: left less the kept room, roomUsdMicro}.
  - Why half: keeping more would leave the work less than its review. The work then runs with all that is left (the owner's 'it should get done anyway'), and its review waits for Continue if it does not fit (BA-3).
- The runner sets PlanItem.reviewRoomUsdMicro (append-only) before each work run, from planner.reviewPartOf(task) (append-only, beside wholeEstimateOf, runner.ts:4946) and the critic port.
- runCapSource comes from the work cap: 'task_budget' when left less the room is at most the session's work budget left, else 'session' (executor.ts:1005). A task_budget pause's cap is the budget, its 'may spend' figure is the work cap (executor.ts:1767-1795), and the brief's budget is the work cap (:1049).
- runCapOf stays 'what is left of the budget' for TaskView.cap. The session's work budget left still caps the run, and the tiny-budget rule (ADR 0112 point 4) applies to the work cap.
- Words, only when a room is kept (no clause when nothing is kept, so no promise the code does not keep; BA-12 warns instead):
  - start line: 'This run may spend CHF 0.70 (CHF 0.10 of the task's budget is kept for its review): before a step that could take it past CHF 0.56 it is told to wrap up, keeping a reserve of CHF 0.14 to finish.' The clause follows the amount in every form of budgetLineWords;
  - a hard stop at the work cap: 'The run stopped at its budget of CHF 0.80, less the CHF 0.10 kept for its review: it spent CHF 0.70, and its next step would have gone over.';
  - a wrap-up pause: '...: it spent CHF 0.56 and listed 2 things left to do; CHF 0.10 is kept for its review.';
  - its card's first sentence: 'It spent CHF 0.56 of its budget of CHF 0.80, keeping CHF 0.10 for its review.' (request-words.ts pausedSpendSentence, from the card's append-only room_usd_micro).
- When nothing is left and the critic sent the task back (attempt > 0 with open findings), the summary reads 'The critic sent it back, and its budget of CHF 0.20 is spent (CHF 0.20 so far): Continue in the Inbox gives it more for the changes the critic asked for.' A first run keeps 'Its budget of CHF 0.20 is spent (CHF 0.20 so far), so nothing ran.' Both file one card with Continue.
- A task without a budget of its own keeps its specialist's limit per run with no room (its review is the session's).
Why: the owner's 'wrap up in an organized and error free way'. A task whose budget holds its work and its review gets reviewed inside it. The room is sized from what the hooks check, not from what a review usually costs.

BA-5 One Continue at the task's own budget covers what is left.
- When the card is filed at task_budget, it stores needs_usd_micro (append-only), never below 0:
  - a work pause: the whole estimate left before the budget cap (estimateLeftUsdMicro(whole estimate, kept work) without withinTaskBudget), plus W, less what is left;
  - a review that waits: R plus the larger of the refused call's estimateUsdMicro (BA-3) and W, less what is left. The 'not started' case uses W.
- Continue at task_budget gives the larger of 'the same amount again' and needs_usd_micro, in CHF 0.01 steps.
- The session-budget branch (OP-6) is unchanged, and a card without needs_usd_micro (filed before) answers as today.
Why: needs follows the same R + W rule as the room, so one Continue lets the review's calls pass the precheck: no second card for the same review, and nothing added beyond what the button says.

BA-6 Every estimate includes the review and, through the learned ratios, the fixes.
- EstimateModel.estimate() returns the work part unchanged, plus a review part. The work part is the task's own estimate or the starting figure times the size factor, times the learned work ratio, whose samples already include every fix run.
- The review part is REVIEW_STARTING_ESTIMATES_USD_MICRO for the task's review tier, times the size factor, times a learned review ratio for the same (specialist, kind) key. The review tier is reviewTierOf(risk_tier, the specialist's registry floor), the critic's own rule (loop/verification.ts:28-31).
- The starting figures: tier 1 USD 0.03, tier 2 USD 0.09, tier 3 USD 0.30 (docs/status/COST.md:150-151: 80 tier 1 reviews cost USD 2.01; gates.md D.12 and D.15; live check 3: tier 1 reviews of USD 0.011 to 0.048).
- EstimateResult gains reviewUsdMicro (part of usdMicro), and the exported pure reviewPartUsdMicro(input, floor) is what the fake daemon uses.
- The stored est_cost_usd_micro stays the work part, so the intake's bounded guess, every stored row and every learned work sample stay valid, with no marker or migration. TaskView.estimate stays that stored work part; no screen shows it, and api-types.ts says so.
- The registry floor reaches the model through EstimateModelOptions.reviewFloor (compose.ts's estimate hunk). A task for the person keeps 0. startingEstimates: null with no reviewStartingEstimates gives no review part.
- Every figure goes through planEstimateUsdMicro: the plan line, the Start dialog, the plan card, the planner, priceNow and the pause card's estimate show one figure that includes the review (R-estimates). withinTaskBudget caps the whole at what is left.
- The intake card's stored sentence ('a first-session plan of N task(s) (~CHF x)') and its 'First session: 1. X (~CHF y)' lines stop naming a figure (intake.ts:1453-1457, :1466-1472, :1491). The card's rows and its total are the daemon's figures (InboxPage.tsx:350-370, W15-72), the one place for them.
- keptWorkOf is unchanged: reviews are never kept work, and a send-back still starts over in the planner's figure (ADR 0115 point 4).
- The session's work budget, its fifth and the plan's cut stay. workRemainingUsdMicro already counts all spend, reviews included (budget.ts:318-326), so whole estimates make the cut honest. A session therefore plans fewer tasks for the same budget, and the user guide and CHANGELOG say so.
Why: the session lead's reading, 'its estimate includes the reviews and fixes', with the R-estimates rule kept.

BA-7 One sample per task, the same in both feeds and across restarts.
- The sample is a pure function of the task's final rows.
  - Work part: as today (workCostOf, every exclusion of isNoSample).
  - Review part: its actual is the cost of the task's critic Run rows (RunTally.reviews). There is no review sample when one of them ran in fast mode, stopped at a budget or was killed.
  - Its time is the latest updated_at of the task's finished Run rows.
- The model keeps the samples by task id. A task's new sample replaces its old one, and that key's state is rebuilt by replaying its samples in time order (then task id). The fold after a restart builds the same samples and replays them the same way. So a task that closes twice (done, Redo, done; failed, Try again, done; Reopen), or that a refresh reads again after the merge watcher patched it, counts once, with its final rows.
- The live feed: the runner calls onTaskFinished once, at the task's close (done, failed after its tries, cancelled; after the verdict that closes it), no longer at every task.finished event. compose's hook body is unchanged; only its comment changes.
- refresh(store) (EstimatePort.refresh?, optional) runs before GET /projects/:id/start-check prices and before a request view prices plan tasks (server.ts). So a task closed outside a session (Inbox Mark done anyway or Cancel, chat, the merge watcher) is learned before the next Start dialog and plan card. It never runs between the dialog and the plan that Start writes (S-8).
- The snapshot goes to version 3; no stored snapshot exists outside tests.
Why: validation rule 4 and W15-19. With reviews and fixes in the sample, the live figures must equal the fold's after a restart.

BA-8 The session review sets the planned tasks' whole cost against the plan's estimate.
- setPlan marks a plan whose estimates include reviews (plan.counts = 'all').
- For a marked plan, the compared figure is the ledger rows of the session whose task id is a planned task. The rest of the session's spend (the task check, lesson reviews; task_id null) is named apart and never counted in the overrun.
- Finding: 'Planned tasks cost CHF 0.17, over their estimate of CHF 0.05 by 240%', with run L3's ', with one task tried twice' / 'tried N times' / 'N tasks tried again'.
- Summary: '... cost CHF 0.22 (the planned tasks CHF 0.20 against an estimate of CHF 0.19, the session's own checks CHF 0.02); ...', or '... cost CHF 0.20 against an estimate of CHF 0.19; ...' when nothing else was spent.
- Metrics line: 'Session review measured: 1 of 2 planned tasks done; the planned tasks cost CHF 0.10 against an estimate of CHF 0.23.', with ', and the session's own checks CHF 0.02' when more than 0. The metrics carry counts 'all', tasksUsdMicro and otherUsdMicro.
- A plan or metrics row without the mark (written before, or a session recovered after the upgrade) keeps today's work-against-work words, read as written.
Why: one figure against an estimate that counts it; no false overrun from spend no plan item estimates; and 'it' no longer reads as the review.

BA-9 The screens show one figure against the budget.
- taskCapWords for a task budget reads 'of CHF 0.20 budget' under the cost while the cost is below the budget, and 'CHF 0.20 budget used up' when TaskView.cap is 0 or the cost reaches the budget. It never reads 'CHF 0.00' or 'reviews are not counted'. Its tooltip: 'Its work, the critic's reviews and any fixes all count. The task pauses at this budget and keeps its work.' The specialist-limit branch is unchanged.
- TaskView.spent and Costs > By task read one new append-only method, costLedger.byTaskOf(projectId, {from, to}): the ledger's rows by task id for the tasks now in this project, with no project filter. A task Make one project moved keeps its whole figure on its row, in the drawer and under By task. The totals and the other buckets stay project-filtered, and OJ-07's 'spent before it joined' line is unchanged. api-types.ts's field docs say actual and spent are that one figure.
- At the cut line: the drawer header reads '... · spent CHF 0.13 of CHF 0.20 budget' from the same helper, and the New task and Edit budget hints read 'Its work, the critic's reviews and any fixes count. Empty: each run stops at its specialist's limit.'
Why: the owner's answer as read ('the Tasks row, the drawer and Costs show one figure against the budget'); design §5 rules 7 and 10.

BA-10 The fake daemon stays in step with the real one, in the same commits.
- Its budgeted fixtures (apps/ui/test/fixtures.ts:235-266; fake-tasks.ts has none) have actual equal to spent.
- fakePrice adds the review part through the runtime's exported reviewPartUsdMicro, and Continue counts from the total (fake-daemon.ts:930-937 and its Continue answer).
- Its TaskView cap is the budget less the total.
Why: validation rule 3.

BA-11 What counts and what stays out, decided by the owner's intent ('the budget is what the task costs') and asserted; no new mechanism.
- These count: Redo, Try again and a conflict or rebuild card's Redo (the same task row: its figure is never reset or raised by them; a Redo with nothing left pauses before it runs with one card and Continue); a retry after a failed run and the ladder's stand-in; web searches (priced in the call); a call Stop now cut off; late usage; an SDK run's subagents.
- These stay out, as session or project spend: C4's task check (no task id), the session review, the critic's lesson reviews, the critic's monthly check, planning and chat.
- C4's task.split shares 'budget less actual', which after BA-1 is what is left after the work and the reviews, with no code change.
- Nothing is booked, so nothing counts, for: the critic's checks and tries, the kept-work check, rebuilds, conflict handling and the merge step.

BA-12 (cut line) The Start dialog warns when a budgeted task's budget cannot hold its work and its review: what is left is below its whole estimate plus W. StartCheck gains reviewMayWait[] (append-only), and the dialog shows one line per task: '"Add a footer line with the club's name to index.html": its budget of CHF 0.10 may leave too little for its review, which then waits for Continue.' The task still runs. Why: answer 8, 'it should get a warning, but it should get done anyway'. If cut, it goes to the leftovers with this wording.
u_entries:
U-042 (open, docs/status/UPDATE-LOG.md:72: 'The budget set on a task is never enforced ... The task's budget is the cap.') carries this change. Run L3 filed no U-entry for L3-run-3. The session lead adds 'd1116-budget-all (C4b)' to its areas, with this Check in the app step:
1. New task: a coder task 'Add a footer line with the club's name to index.html' with Budget 0.10, and a coder task 'Add a contact line with the club's email to index.html' with Budget 1.00. The Start dialog prices the first at CHF 0.10 or less.
2. Press Start. The second task's start line says what it keeps for its review ('(CHF 0.10 of the task's budget is kept for its review)'); the first task's says nothing of it.
3. For the first task, one of three things happens:
   - (a) it is reviewed and done within CHF 0.10;
   - (b) the log says '"Add a footer line with the club's name to index.html" paused before its review: its own budget of CHF 0.10 has no room for it.', the second task still runs, and the Inbox card says 'The work is done; its review waits for room in the budget.' with Continue (CHF N more). Continue runs only the critic, the task is done, and no second card comes;
   - (c) its work pauses at its budget with a card and Continue.
4. Each Tasks row reads its cost with 'of CHF x budget' under it, the same figure as the drawer and Costs > By task. Hovering it shows 'Its work, the critic's reviews and any fixes all count. The task pauses at this budget and keeps its work.' No screen says 'reviews are not counted'.
5. If the critic sends a task back, the task never reads more than its budget before a Continue.
No new U-entry. The session lead may add one if it wants the owner's answer tracked on its own; the area does not take a number.

final.adr:
ADR 0112 (a budget stop is a clean pause) gets a dated amendment appended at the end: "Amendment 2026-11-16 (run C, C4b, 'd1116-budget-all'): a task's budget counts its reviews and fixes", quoting the owner verbatim ("yes it should count critics reviews, and fixes.").

1. **One figure.** actual_cost_usd_micro is everything spent on the task: its work runs, every review of them (each call as it ends) and the fixes. It equals the ledger's sum for the task. Migration 0010 counts old tasks the same way.
2. **The review is capped.** A task's review stops at what is left of the task's own budget.
- Below the price of the review's output cap alone, the critic is not started.
- A refusal there is the task's budget: one card with review_waits and Continue, and the session goes on.
- The refused call's estimate is kept on the card.
- After Continue, the review runs without the specialist.
- At effort max, the first call's output ceiling is sized from that room too (decided; the floor of 8,192 is unchanged).
3. **Room for the review.** Each work run, a fix included, keeps R + W when that is at most half of what is left:
- R is the review part of its estimate;
- W is one critic call's worst case at its tier, model and output cap, with an input allowance of 8,000 tokens beside the prompt.
Otherwise it keeps nothing and the work runs with all that is left. The run's cap source is its own cap. This is the task's twin of point 7; point 7 itself (the session's fifth) stays.
4. **Continue.** At the task's own budget, Continue gives at least what the task still needs: its estimate left plus W for a work pause, and R plus the larger of the refused estimate and W for a waiting review, less what is left.
5. **Estimates.** Estimates include the review: a review part by review tier and size, learned per kind. They include the fixes through the learned ratios. Each task is one sample, kept by task id and replaced when it closes again, in both feeds.
6. **The session review** sets the planned tasks' cost against a plan marked counts 'all', and names the session's own checks apart.

findings.problem: The room each work run keeps for its review is min(a fifth of what is left, the review part of the estimate). The review part is what a review is expected to cost. But the critic's precheck refuses any call whose worst case passes the run's cap, and the worst case is the whole input plus 8,192 output tokens. So whenever a work run spends up to its work cap, which is the case BA-4 exists for, the kept room never fits the review's first call and the review always waits. At CHF 0.06 (USD 0.075) the first call's worst case is more than the whole budget. The U-042 step's 'or the task is done within it' and LC-C32's first branch cannot happen. No screen warns that such a budget can never pay for a review, although answer 8 asks for a warning.

map.summary: Today a task's budget counts only the specialist's work runs, and fix rounds are among them. The critic's reviews are booked everywhere except on the task. Fixes already count: every work run, the runs after a send-back included, adds its cost to task.actual_cost_usd_micro (runner.ts:2428-2436 per call, runner.ts:2546-2551 rest at the end, executor.ts:2456-2479 late usage). The next run's cap is budget less that figure (runCapOf, executor.ts:696-706, used at executor.ts:977-1049). Reviews do not count. The critic's runs carry the task's id on their token (critic.ts:496-515), their ledger rows (hooks.ts:256-282) and their Run rows (specialist 'critic', critic.ts:637-663). So the session budget, the project budget, the monthly cap, Costs > By task and TaskView.spent already include them (budget.ts:380-388, caps.ts:177-189 and DynamicCaps compose.ts:1442-1472, server.ts:1102-1113, runner.ts:3410-3411 and 3720). Two gaps remain. Nothing adds a review to actual: reviewTask (runner.ts:4341-4439) only puts outcome.costUsdMicro on the event row. And the review's run cap is the session token's whole budget (runner.ts:1158-1176 and 2779-2794; loop/critic.ts:686-714 passes no budgetUsdMicro; critic.ts:507), so a review can never stop at the task's budget. 'Work only' is not decided in one place. It follows from where task.addCost is called, plus two separate CRITIC_RUN_SPECIALIST constants (estimates/model.ts:309-310, critic/session-review.ts:105-106) used by the learner and the session review. Run L3 made no engine change. It changed only the words: TasksTab.tsx:74-99 and ADR 0112:479-490, which says 'Making the task's budget count the reviews too is an engine change the owner has not asked for'. The change has five parts. (1) Book every review call on the task as the call ends. (2) Cap each review at what is left of the task's budget, and name its refusal as the task's budget: today the refusal comes as level 'run', and reviewStopSource maps 'run' to 'session' (runner.ts:969-982). (3) Have each work run, fixes included, keep room in the task's budget for the review that follows. This is the task-level twin of ADR 0112 point 7. Without it, nearly every task that works close to its budget pauses before its review. That is clean (TR-14/W15-27 keep the result and later review it without a rerun), but it adds a card. (4) Make estimates include reviews; fixes are already in the learned samples. (5) Make the session review and the screens compare one figure with the budget and the estimate. The session work budget is already measured on all spend, reviews included (budget.ts:318-326, 365-371). Estimates that include reviews therefore make the plan cut (runner.ts:1512, 2096-2104; start-check.ts:230) more consistent, not less, and the session reserve can stay. Not task spend, recommended to stay out: the task check on step 4's branch (no task id, task-check.ts:462-528 there), the session review, promotion reviews, planning and chat. Rebuilds, merges, kept-work checks and the critic's checks and tries book nothing. Redo, Try again, conflict Redo and continued runs are work runs and already count. The main practical risk is small budgets. A light review's first call is priced at its 8,192-token output cap on Sonnet: USD 0.082 of output alone, before input (critic.ts:134, ladder.ts:160-167, pricing.ts:104). Live check 3 measured about CHF 0.04 for one light review (ADR 0112:482-484). A CHF 0.20 task can therefore pause before its review unless the work leaves room for it or the review's first call is sized to the room.

risks_and_edge_cases: Small budgets: a light review's first call is priced at 8,192 output tokens on Sonnet, USD 0.082 of output alone (critic.ts:134; ladder.ts:160-167; pricing.ts:104). Opus reviews at tiers 2 and 3 cost twice the output price (ladder.ts:169-176; pricing.ts:105). Once reviews count, a CHF 0.20 task can pause before every review unless the work keeps room or the review's first call shrinks to the room. Live check 3 measured about CHF 0.04 for one light review (ADR 0112:482-484). The live 'Swiss pairing tool' task cost USD 0.21 of work alone (estimates/model.ts:178-180) against a USD 0.25 budget.
Double counting: book reviews per call on the task and add nothing from outcome.costUsdMicro at the end. The runner's end-of-run rest (runner.ts:2550-2551) must stay work-run-only.
A review refused halfway (no verdict) spends money for nothing, and its review-only pass pays again. A room check before the review starts avoids it.
Restart between the ledger row and task.addCost leaves actual below the ledger. That gap exists today for work steps too. Reading max(actual, ledger by task) at run start closes it.

The run-level refusal of a review capped at the task's budget arrives as level 'run'. Today that maps to 'session' (runner.ts:969-982): the card would name the session's budget and the session would end (stopEndsSession).
A continued task: if the review room were a share of the whole budget (as the session's is), a task with large past spend would get a run cap of zero after Continue. Use a share of what is left.
Existing tasks: their actual excludes past reviews. A backfill makes some tasks pause at once after the upgrade; leaving it means one rule for old work and another for new.

Learner transition: stored est_cost (work only, set by the intake, intake.ts:2304 and 2731) measured against whole-task samples would push the learned ratio up, and the reviews would then be counted twice in new estimates. Learning reviews as their own figure avoids this.
Step 4's task.split (fix/d1109-selftasks-run task.ts:2127-2146) shares budget less actual. With work-only actual it shares money the reviews already spent.
Make one project (fix/d1109-onerepo-join) moves task rows and keeps ledger rows' task_id; a ledger-by-task figure still holds after a join.
Subscription runs are booked in the ledger at API prices (sdk.ts:360-366), so budgets in CHF apply to them the same way. The plan share stays its own limit.
Tasks without their own budget (specialist limit per run): under the recommendation nothing changes, and their reviews stay under the session's budget and reserve.

The plan's cut stays against the session's work budget (cap less 20%). That budget is already measured on all spend, reviews included (budget.ts:318-326), so estimates that include reviews make the cut consistent, not doubled. More tasks will read as larger than the session's work budget (D4 path).
Continue at a review that waits: 'the same amount again' (budget-card.ts:56-86) asks for a whole budget when only the review needs room. Nothing is spent beyond what runs, but the number looks large.
The review-only pass's plan line still names the work's estimate (L3 money-engine not_done). A review estimate is needed anyway for the estimates change.
Ownership: runner.ts, executor.ts, request-words.ts and task-check.ts are d1109-cred-engine's only in C5 (runC-plan.json sub_runs C5 note). Editing them in parallel conflicts.
Words in tests and docs fixed by run L3 ('reviews are not counted', 'are not in the estimate') must change together: UI tests, the real-daemon tests, critic tests, the user guide and critic.md.
open_points: A task without a budget of its own (the specialist's limit per run): should its reviews count against anything per task? Recommended: no. The owner spoke of 'a task's budget'; those reviews stay under the session's budget and reserve as today.

How much room a work run keeps for its review: a fifth of what is left (the session's rule, one constant), the learned cost of a review at the task's level, or none (let the review pause with its card). Recommended: the larger of a fifth of what is left and the learned review figure.

Past reviews of existing tasks: backfill them into the budget (one rule; some tasks pause after the upgrade) or count reviews only from the upgrade on. Recommended: backfill, with one CHANGELOG line and the card's words.

Continue for a review that waits at the task's budget: keep 'the same amount again' (ADR 0112 budget-resume point 5) or ask for the review's figure only. Recommended: keep one rule, unless the owner wants smaller asks.
The critic's first call on small rooms: shrink its output cap to the room, or warn in New task when the budget is below the task's estimate with its review. A design choice for the critic area.

The task check (d1109-selftasks-run), the session review, promotion reviews, planning and chat: recommended to stay out of every task's budget. Confirm, since 'the budget is what the task costs' could be read wider for a task check that one task's report triggered.

Redo, Try again and a conflict card's Redo: recommended to count against the same budget, as now. A Redo after the budget is used pauses at once with Continue. Confirm that Redo should not reset or raise the budget.
Sequencing: this change touches runner.ts and executor.ts, which C5's d1109-cred-engine owns alone. Run it after C5 merges, as its own area in C6, or inside C5.

map.summary: Today a task's estimate covers one attempt of the specialist's work and nothing else. A task with no estimate of its own starts from the calibrated work figure per specialist (packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts:146-169). The comment at :153-154 says outright: "It is the work's cost (what the task's budget caps); the critic's review is paid from the session's review reserve". That figure is multiplied by the size factor (:224-251). A task with its own estimate uses the plan model's guess, kept within 1.5x of the work band (:268-280, written by intake.ts:2717-2746). Either base is then multiplied by a ratio learned per (specialist, tier) (:615-652). The learner also measures the work only. tallyRun puts critic Run rows in `reviews` and returns before the fast-mode check (:425-431). workCostOf subtracts them from the ledger (:460-462), in the fold (:780) and in the live feed (:867-868). Fix rounds reach the learner's actual (later work runs are summed) but never the estimate. A task the critic sent back is priced at its whole estimate again: keptWorkOf drops critic runs and counts only paused runs (:926-940), pinned by estimates.test.ts:1075-1083 and ADR 0115:55-63, although the fix really continues on the PR branch (packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:1092-1128). Every figure the person sees goes through one function, planEstimateUsdMicro (:887-906): the plan card (daemon/server.ts:2086-2090 to plan-tasks.ts:133-155), the Start dialog (start-check.ts:190-202), the planner (runner.ts:4941-4991), priceNow (runner.ts:4290-4300) and the pause card (runner.ts:4229-4255). So R-estimates still holds if the review part is added inside EstimateModel.estimate() from inputs every caller already passes: the risk tier, plus the specialist's registry floor wired into the model's options. Several places compare figures against work only: the session review (packages/critic/src/session-review.ts:322-378, 709-716), the metrics line (daemon/views.ts:757-761), withinTaskBudget and runCapOf (budget less actual_cost_usd_micro, which today is work only: model.ts:980-987, executor.ts:696-705), Continue (budget-card.ts:71-86) and the pause card's "more than its estimate" (request-words.ts:844-852). A second structural point: plans are cut against the session's work budget, cap x 0.8 (runner.ts:1511-1515, start-check.ts:230). The fifth held back is the review reserve, which billing calls "kept for review and fixes" (packages/billing/src/caps.ts:171). If each task's estimate holds its own review and fixes, that cut counts reviews twice. Measured review costs by tier: tier 1 (Sonnet, medium) about USD 0.0125 to 0.048 (docs/status/gates.md:157-158, docs/status/COST.md:150-151, /tmp/frbench/live3-result.json:339,609); tier 2 (Opus, high) about USD 0.08 to 0.09; tier 3 (Opus, max) about USD 0.22 to 0.34 (gates.md:160). Live check 3's Swiss task cost CHF 0.12 of work plus CHF 0.06 of reviews against "about CHF 0.11" (live3-result.json:332). A whole-cost starting figure, (USD 0.04 work + USD 0.03 tier-1 review) x 3.55 (the Swiss task's size factor), comes to about CHF 0.20, against the measured CHF 0.18. The live learner has a timing problem. It samples at task.finished (runner.ts:2605-2619), before the review (runner.ts:2780), once per try (model.ts:854-855), and refresh() is never called after start (model.ts:736 is the only caller). Once reviews and fixes count, the live figures would differ from the post-restart fold, the W15-19 class. Recommendation, in the owner's words "the budget is what the task costs": one whole-cost estimate = (work start + review start by review tier) x size, corrected by a learner whose samples are the task's whole ledger total, taken once when the task closes. Tasks written before the change, whose est_cost_usd_micro counts work only, need a marker. Settle the session-reserve question before any figure changes.

changes_needed.risk: A hook after the verdict must also run for the review-only pass (today skipped at runner.ts:2605) and must never sample a task twice (remember()/folded, model.ts:709-720)

changes_needed.change: Replace the kept-work rule with 'spent since the last start over'. After a send-back the fix continues on the task's branch, so the work and reviews spent since the last start over (a Redo from base, a failed run tried again, whose leftovers are set aside) count against the whole estimate. Tell a send-back apart from a Redo by the review decision after the latest work run (Review rows or the critic Run row with verdict revise/retry) and by the redo-from-base marker. Floor what is left at the larger of ESTIMATE_PASSED_SHARE x estimate and one review start, so the review always has room. Amend ADR 0115 point 4.
changes_needed.why: Once the estimate holds the expected fixes, pricing a sent-back task at its whole estimate again counts the fix twice. Live check 3 priced the retry at 'about CHF 0.10' after CHF 0.09 of work and a review (live3-result.json:445, 609). A fix continues on the PR branch (pr-executor.ts:1092-1128); only a Redo or a failed try starts over (pr-executor.ts:1190-1211)
changes_needed.risk: ADR 0115 warned that pricing at estimate less earlier spend lets join-if-fits admit a task that does not fit. The floor (a fifth, at least one review) and withinTaskBudget keep that bounded, but a conservative alternative is a learned 'fix round' figure per key with a starting value of the whole work start (today's behaviour)

changes_needed.change: withinTaskBudget must subtract everything the task has spent (work, reviews, fixes), not the work-only actual_cost_usd_micro. Either the engine makes actual_cost_usd_micro the whole (critic runs also call task.addCost), or withinTaskBudget reads the ledger sum (TaskView.spent). Use the same figure in runCapOf.
changes_needed.why: An estimate may never be above what the budget has left (U-042), and the budget now counts reviews
changes_needed.risk: Owned by the engine part. Both sides must use one figure, or the Start dialog and the run's 'This run may spend' line disagree again (L3-run-3)

changes_needed.change: Keep the task's own review out of what its work run may spend. The run's cap is (budget left) less the review estimate of its tier, using the same review-estimate function as the model, so the run's wrap-up leaves room for its review.
changes_needed.why: A task whose work spends to its budget leaves its review no room. It then pauses before its review ('paused before its review'), which is the pause ADR 0112 wants to avoid when the estimate fits
changes_needed.risk: On tiny budgets the reserve may exceed the cap. ADR 0112 point 4's tiny-budget rule must state what applies

changes_needed.change: Decide the session review reserve (see open point 1). Recommended: once each task's estimate holds its own review and fixes, plans, re-plans, the Start check, the promise, followers and the plan card's 'larger than a session' note compare whole estimates with the session's budget less only a small reserve for session-level spend (session review, task check, promotion review), not with cap x 0.8. Continue at the session's budget drops the division by (1 - reserve).
changes_needed.why: Otherwise every review is counted twice, once in each task's estimate and once in the fifth held back. Tasks that fit would be left out, and Continue would ask for more than needed
changes_needed.risk: It touches the engine's hard caps (another part) and every 'work budget' sentence. If the reserve is kept unchanged instead, the plan must cut only the work part of each estimate against the work budget, a two-part figure the screens must never show apart

changes_needed.change: Continue (CHF N more) at the task's own budget or the specialist's limit: at least what is left of the whole estimate (the card's estimate_left_usd_micro), not the raw est_cost_usd_micro. Then Continue covers the rest of the work and its review.

risks_and_edge_cases: Double counting with the session's review reserve: estimates holding reviews, cut against cap x 0.8 (runner.ts:1511-1515, start-check.ts:230), count each review twice. Fewer tasks fit, and Continue at the session's budget asks for left / 0.8 (budget-card.ts:79-82).

Historical rows: est_cost_usd_micro of every task written so far is work only, and the learner refolds all finished tasks at start (model.ts:731-738). Without a marker or lift, every learned ratio jumps about 1.5-2x the first time the new code starts.

Live vs fold divergence (W15-19 class, validation rule 4): the live hook samples before the review (runner.ts:2605-2619 vs :2780) and per try (model.ts:854-855). Once reviews count, a restart would move the plan card and Start dialog figures.
Tasks closed outside the runner (Mark done anyway, Cancel in the Inbox) are learned only at the next restart: refresh() is only called from fromStore (model.ts:736).

A run that spends to its budget leaves no room for its review, so the task pauses 'before its review' at its own budget unless the run's cap holds back the review estimate (executor.ts:977-1000, engine part).
Tiny budgets: the review reserve can be larger than the whole budget (for example a CHF 0.02 budget against a USD 0.03 tier-1 review). ADR 0112 point 4's tiny-budget rule must say what happens.
A fast-mode critic run is not flagged: tallyRun returns before isFastModeVariant for critic rows (model.ts:428-434), so the surcharge would enter samples once reviews count.

Splits (C4 d1109-selftasks-run): each part has its own review, so the parts' whole estimates sum to more than the whole's. The branch's 'part's room comes out of the whole's estimate' rule under-counts.

Telling a send-back fix apart from a Redo from base is not possible from Run rows alone: both have a 'completed' latest work run (estimates.test.ts:1070-1083). It needs the review decision or the redo marker.

The estimate model's key (specialist, tier) does not hold the project's critic_ceiling or effort slider (packages/critic/src/model.ts:85-100), which change the review's model. Two projects with different ceilings share one learned ratio.

Tier escalation: the fourth attempt runs one rung up (loop/ports.ts:266-280) and the review tier can escalate (loop/critic.ts:854), so a long ladder costs well over the mean. The per-sample clamp of 10x (model.ts:314-315) and the median-like EWMA bound one outlier.

R-estimates: the plan card's estimate.of (plan-tasks.ts:146-152) passes no outcome or criteria and relies on est_cost_usd_micro > 0. If the review part is added outside estimate() in one caller only, the plan card and the Start dialog disagree again (leftovers7-session).
Old session plans reviewed after the upgrade (orphan recovery) must keep the work-against-work comparison, or they file false overruns.
The Swiss review-to-size evidence is two live data points (live3-result.json:339, 609); scaling the review by size is weakly supported.
open_points: Session review reserve (decide first): keep the fifth of every session held for reviews, or, now that each task's estimate holds its review and fixes, plan whole estimates against the session's budget and reserve only each running task's own review (plus a small session-level reserve for the session review, the task check and promotion reviews)? Recommendation: the second, following the owner's 'the budget is what the task costs'. It touches the engine's caps (billing/src/caps.ts:167-172, enforcement/budget.ts:318-370), the plan cut, the Start dialog, Continue and the 'budget less a fifth kept for reviews' words.

Expected fix rounds at cold start: recommend none in the starting figure (factor 1), learned from samples that now include fixes. A documented starting share needs data: the Run rows of the live-check homes can give the send-back rate (live phase 1 had 3 of 3 accepted with no retries, docs/status/gates.md:24; live check 3's Swiss task was sent back once, live3-result.json:332).

Which finished tasks are samples: today done, failed and cancelled (model.ts:287). With reviews and fixes counted, a task that exhausted the ladder (4 attempts, 4 reviews) and was then cancelled pushes estimates up. Recommend done tasks plus failed ones, leaving out cancelled tasks whose last review was not an accept. Owner-visible effect is small; session lead to confirm.

The figure for a task the critic sent back: (a) estimate less work and reviews since the last start over, floored at max(a fifth, one review start) (recommended), or (b) a learned 'fix round' figure starting at the whole work start, today's caution in ADR 0115 point 4.

Wall time: should the estimate's time (and the Performance time ratio) also count the reviews' durations? Today it is work runs only (model.ts:439). Not required by the owner's words, which are about money.
Retries after a failed run and Redo are not clearly 'fixes'. Recommend counting them, since they are counted in the budget today and are what the task costs; confirm with the session lead.
The task check (C4), the session review, promotion reviews, intake and chat: recommend keeping them out of task budgets (session or project spend), since none is one task's work or review.
Marker storage for 'this estimate counts everything': a task column (next migration after C4's 0009) or a plan-row field. Choose with the C4 and C5 owners to avoid a migration-number clash.

risks_and_edge_cases: A task's run must leave room in the task's budget for its review. Otherwise a tight budget runs the work to the line, pauses 'before its review', and Continue only then pays the review: two cards for one task. C4b decides the share (a fifth, as the session's reserve, or the review's estimate).

Reviews must not be counted twice. If the estimates include reviews while the plan cut, the promise and the admit room still compare them with the session's work budget (the cap less the fifth: start-check.ts:230-238, runner.ts:1512-1516, :1821-1822), fewer tasks fit. That goes against option C ('spare budget isn't wasted'). The hooks' fifth (budget.ts:318-326; requirement I.4) still stays.

Make one project (C4): the Tasks row's figure is read with a projectId filter (server.ts:1102-1106), while the closing project's ledger rows stay where they are (runC-plan.json:1060). A moved task's budget figure would drop its earlier spend. Undo moves it back.

The learner: samples become work plus reviews plus fixes, so a send-back roughly doubles a sample and CL-15's swings grow. The stored snapshot (model.ts:343-351, version 2) and the fold must agree after a restart (ADR 0112's 'restarting the app changes none of these figures'). Learning the review part separately per kind keeps the swing down.

A review refused at the task's own budget names the wrong limit. SessionBudget's run-cap refusal reports level 'run' (budget.ts:338-348), and reviewStopSource maps only 'task' to task_budget (runner.ts:969-982), so the card would say 'the session's budget'.
Cards filed before the change carry spent_usd_micro with the work only (budget-card.ts:250). Their words keep reading as filed; do not recompute them as 'in all'.

Tasks without a budget of their own: each work run still stops at the specialist's limit per run, and their reviews go to the session's spend. The owner spoke of 'a task's budget', so the row's 'each run stops at CHF 2.40 (the coder's limit)' stays.
Redo, Try again and a conflict card's Redo continue the same task row and its budget, so a task whose budget is already used pauses at once. Say it where the person presses.
The task check (C4) and chat's 'fix the tasks' (C6) must not reduce the budget of the task whose report triggered them. They stay session or project spend.

The session review's whole cost includes the task check (session spend, specialist 'task-check'), which no plan estimate covers. It is small, but it can tip an overrun finding; keep it apart or below the noise line (session-review.ts:101-104).
On the subscription the ledger books calls at API-equivalent prices. The task's figure then mixes credentials in one sum, which is consistent with CS-9's 'your subscription as its estimate'.
The C4 branches are unfinished. Line numbers on fix/d1109-selftasks-run and fix/d1109-onerepo-join will move before C4 merges.
Live check 4: the real critic's send-back is not deterministic, so the priority-1 step should be the review that does not fit (deterministic), with the send-back case observed when it happens.

Requirement I.4 says the session reserve is 'for review and fixes' (docs/requirements.md:153; caps.ts:37), but fixes are work runs capped at the work share (executor.ts:996-1002). Wording a person reads must not promise that the reserve pays fixes.
open_points: How the work run keeps room for its own review inside the task's budget: a fixed share, the review's learned estimate, or none (pause before the review). This is an engine design choice the plan does not cover.

How the estimate gains its review part: a learned review cost per kind, a fixed share, or the ledger's total as the sample. And whether the plan, the promise and the admit room are then measured against the whole session budget or still the work budget.
Area key, sub-run name and wave (proposed 'd1116-task-budget', 'C4b', wave 24) are the session lead's choice. Phases E's pipeline runs one sub-run per call, so a one-key sub-run works.
